claims.text: The unmodified Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy has limited amorphous retention.
The unmodified alloy exhibits early and complex crystallization behavior during reheating.
Adding approximately 2 at.% boron will enhance glass formation in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Adding approximately 2 at.% boron will improve the alloy's thermal stability during reheating.
The proposed modified composition is Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P18B2.
Boron will increase atomic-level disorder and produce a confusion effect.
The increased disorder will disrupt the formation of crystalline nuclei and produce a more robust amorphous structure.
Boron atoms have sufficiently small size and distinct chemical affinities to create local topological and chemical inhomogeneities in this alloy.
Boron-induced local inhomogeneities will raise the nucleation barrier against crystalline-phase formation during cooling.
Boron-induced disorder will delay crystallization during reheating.
After otherwise identical quenching, the boron-modified alloy will retain a higher amorphous fraction than the baseline alloy.
During DSC reheating at approximately 20 K/min, the boron-modified alloy will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature than the baseline alloy.
The intervention is expected to be beneficial primarily at moderate to high cooling rates where nucleation suppression is important.
At extremely high cooling rates, the baseline alloy may already become amorphous, reducing the observable benefit of boron.
At very slow cooling rates, 2 at.% boron may be insufficient to prevent crystallization.
Cooling rates of approximately 10^3–10^5 K/s and DSC reheating at 20 K/min under high-purity nitrogen are proposed for testing the intervention.
Failure to increase amorphous fraction by more than 10% or crystallization-onset temperature by about 10 K under identical conditions would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as adding 2 at.% B to the base alloy, but the example composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P18B2 replaces 2 at.% P with B rather than adding B while proportionally renormalizing the original composition.
